en.title: Tail N Lines Preserving Original Text
en.description: Given a string array lines (each element is one line, without a newline character) and a non-negative integer n, return the last n lines in their original order. For n=0, return an empty array; when n exceeds the array length, return all lines.
en.input: The first line contains `lineCount n`. Then, for each line string, first give its UTF-8 byte length L, then on the next line give exactly L raw bytes as the content, immediately followed by an LF separator. A string may be empty and may contain spaces, tabs, and non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, but not LF. 0≤lineCount≤5000, 0≤n≤5000, and the total length of all payload is ≤30000 bytes. This length-prefixed protocol preserves empty lines and in-line whitespace losslessly.
en.output: Output the result with the same length-prefixed protocol: first output the number of returned lines, then for each line output its UTF-8 byte length and raw content; for an empty array, output only `0`.
en.explanation: The source semantics are clear; this site supplements the I/O encoding with UTF-8 byte-length prefixes so that empty strings, spaces, and tabs are not lost in token-based input.
hints: You only need to keep a queue of size at most n; enqueue each new line as you traverse, and remove the earliest line once the capacity is exceeded.
